downstream_reviews.source_excerpt: 1.1 Identify the real Hermitian space with its finite coordinate space. The constant map $P\mapsto h$ has derivative zero. The real-linear map $G$ is continuous by [F9] and has derivative $G$ at every point because $G(P+H)-G(P)-G(H)=0$. By [F7] the first partials of $E_{xc}$ are $C^1$: each has first partials given by the continuous second partials of $E_{xc}$, and [F8] makes each component of $\nabla E_{xc}$ total differentiable with continuous derivative. Thus all three summands in [F1] are $C^1$, so $F$ is $C^1$ and Hermitian-valued on the model's open domain. [given, F1, F2, F7, F8, F9, algebra]

downstream_reviews.source_excerpt: 2.1 Let $S_\varepsilon=LL^*$ be its Cholesky factorization. By [F1], $y=L^*c$ preserves the exact generalized eigenvalues and Rayleigh quotient. For any matrix $A$, $\|A\|_2^2=\max_{\|x\|_2=1}x^*A^*Ax$, which equals the largest eigenvalue of the positive Hermitian matrix $A^*A$ by [F2]. Since $(L^{-1})^*L^{-1}=L^{-*}L^{-1}=S_\varepsilon^{-1}$, its eigenvalues are $1/\varepsilon$ and $1/(2-\varepsilon)$, so $\|L^{-1}\|_2=\varepsilon^{-1/2}$. For $A=L^{-*}$, $A^*A=L^{-1}L^{-*}=L^{-1}S_\varepsilon^{-1}L$, which is similar to $S_\varepsilon^{-1}$; hence $\|L^{-*}\|_2=\varepsilon^{-1/2}$ as well. The operator norm is attained on a unit vector in this finite-dimensional space, so a unit perturbation in a maximizing direction is amplified by this factor when converted back to coefficient coordinates. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

downstream_reviews.source_excerpt:
In $\mathbb C^2$ with $r=1$, let $H=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, $h=0$,
$E_{xc}=0$, and define $G(A)=2\operatorname{tr}(HA)H$ on Hermitian $A$. Then
$G$ is a self-adjoint real-linear map, so it defines the allowed nonlinear
projector energy $E(P)=\operatorname{tr}(HP)^2$. At $P_0=e_1e_1^*$ the
commutator stationarity condition holds, but $P_0$ is a strict local maximum,
not a minimum.

downstream_reviews.source_excerpt:
Let $P_0\in\mathcal P_r$ be stationary for the $C^2$ energy $E$ of
[[def-finite-basis-projector-energy-model]]. Use its graph chart $P(X)$ from
[[lem-rank-r-projector-grassmann-chart-and-tangent]], with $P(0)=P_0$, and put
$\psi(X)=E(P(X))$. If there is $c>0$ such that
$$D^2\psi(0)[X,X]\ge c\|X\|_F^2\quad\text{for every }X:U\to U^\perp,$$
then $P_0$ is a strict isolated local minimum on $\mathcal P_r$. Since
projectors identify frames related by unitary rotations, this is a strict local
minimum modulo orbital gauge. This is a sufficient condition, not a claim that
every stationary point satisfies it.

downstream_reviews.source_excerpt:
Take $n=2$, $r=1$, overlap $S=I_2$, Cholesky factor $L=I_2$, $h=0$, and
$E_{xc}=0$ in [[def-finite-basis-projector-energy-model]]. Define
$G:\mathbb H_2\to\mathbb H_2$ by $G(X)=\operatorname{diag}(X_{11},X_{22})$.
Here matrix-entry labels $1,2$ mean the first and second rows/columns, corresponding to canonical indices $0,1$.
The associated response map is $F(P)=G(P)$. Let
$$P_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_1=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}.$$
For the undamped occupied-projector iteration, $P_0$ and $P_1$ form a strict
two-cycle even though the occupied/unoccupied eigenvalue gap equals $1$ at both
iterates.

downstream_reviews.source_excerpt:
Let $P_0=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$, $P_1=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$, and
$X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$. In the finite-basis model choose
$S=L=I_2$, $h=0$, $E_{xc}=0$, and the real-linear map
$$G(P)=\bigl(\langle P,P_0\rangle_F-\langle P,P_1\rangle_F\bigr)X+\langle P,X\rangle_F(P_0-P_1).$$
At $P_0$ and $P_1$ the commutator residuals are equal and nonzero, making the
two-vector Gram matrix singular. A solver that reports this singular system
uses the specified baseline fallback, even though the exact capped minimizer
exists.
